Choosing the best track and field colleges in the US is not only about finding the team with the latest NCAA trophy.

That helps. But it does not answer the real question: where should you apply?

A 100m sprinter, a 5,000m runner and a hammer thrower should not build the same college list. The right choice depends on your event, personal bests, academic goals, scholarship chances, budget and coach interest.

This guide ranks the top track and field colleges using current NCAA performance, long-term programme strength, event fit, facilities, scholarships, tuition estimates and international student-athlete support.

2027 Update: What Applicants Should Know

For students preparing for 2027 entry, the 2026 NCAA Outdoor Championships provide the latest completed snapshot of current programme strength. Arkansas won the men’s outdoor team title, while Georgia won the women’s outdoor team title. The official NCAA outdoor team scores also showed strong results from Florida, Oregon, USC, Tennessee, LSU, Texas A&M, Washington and other major programmes.

But here’s the thing: one championship year should not control your whole decision.

A college that wins in 2026 may not need your event in 2027. Another college may finish lower nationally but offer better coaching attention, scholarship value and competition opportunities for your specific event.

So this guide uses current results as one ranking factor, not the whole answer.

Quick Answer: What Are the Best Track and Field Colleges in the US?

The best track and field colleges in the US include the University of Arkansas, University of Georgia, University of Oregon, University of Florida, LSU, University of Tennessee, USC, Texas A&M University, Auburn University, Stanford University, University of Washington, University of Texas at Austin, University of New Mexico, Grand Valley State University and West Texas A&M University.

The best college track teams are not always the best fit for every athlete. A lower-ranked programme that needs your exact event can be more useful than a famous team with a crowded roster.

How We Ranked the Best Colleges for Track and Field

We used a student-athlete fit model instead of ranking universities by name recognition alone.

Track and field is event-specific. A college can be excellent for distance runners but weaker for throwers. Another can dominate relays but have limited room for your event group.

Use the ranking as a starting point. Then check your event, cost and coach fit.

Top 10 Track and Field Colleges in the US

These are the top 10 track and field colleges in the US for students who want strong NCAA competition, serious coaching, scholarship potential and long-term academic value.

1. University of Arkansas

Arkansas is one of the strongest track and field colleges in the US because it combines current performance with a deep championship culture.

The Razorbacks are especially strong for sprints, jumps, relays and athletes who want a serious NCAA Division I environment. Their men’s programme sits at the top of the current conversation after winning the 2026 NCAA Outdoor title.

But there is a catch.

A powerful roster means tough internal competition. You may train with elite athletes, but you also have to earn travel spots and championship opportunities. Arkansas is best for athletes who already have strong marks or clear scoring potential.

2. University of Georgia

Georgia is one of the best colleges for track and field, especially on the women’s side.

The programme has strong national results and fits athletes in sprints, jumps, combined events and throws. Georgia’s women’s team strength makes it a major option for students searching for women’s track and field colleges with current championship relevance.

For recruits, the key question is simple: does Georgia need your event in your entry year?

If the answer is yes, it can be one of the best places to develop.

3. University of Oregon

Oregon remains one of the most recognised track colleges in the world.

Hayward Field, TrackTown culture and Oregon’s distance tradition make it a dream option for many runners. Distance and middle-distance athletes should keep Oregon high on the list.

The caution is cost and roster depth. Oregon can be expensive for out-of-state and international students before aid, and the competition for places can be intense.

Students comparing public options should also look at other state-funded universities across the USA before choosing a final shortlist.

4. University of Florida

Florida is one of the best track and field colleges for sprinters, hurdlers and athletes who want elite competition inside a major public university.

The Gators have a strong reputation in speed and technical events. They also offer broad academic choices, which matters if you want athletics and a useful degree path.

Florida is not a casual target. Coaches at this level usually look for athletes who can score at conference level, develop quickly or add depth to a specific event group.

5. Louisiana State University

LSU is a strong choice for sprints, relays and jumps.

The programme has a clear identity: speed, pressure and national-level performance. For relay athletes and short sprinters, LSU is not just a famous name. It is a real event-fit option.

Still, do not apply only because the brand is strong. Ask whether the coaching staff needs your exact event profile.

A powerful programme only helps if there is a lane for you.

6. University of Tennessee

Tennessee has become one of the most important track and field programmes to watch.

It offers SEC competition, strong momentum and a serious NCAA environment. For male athletes in particular, Tennessee deserves attention because of its recent national performance.

Here is a slightly surprising point: a rising programme can sometimes be better for recruitment than the most obvious famous school. Coaches building depth may pay close attention to the right athlete in the right event.

7. University of Southern California

USC is one of the best track and field colleges in California and a strong option for sprints and relays.

It also offers a private university environment in Los Angeles, which can appeal to students thinking about networks, internships and life after athletics.

USC’s cost is high before aid. International students should ask about athletic aid, academic awards, need-based support and total cost after scholarships rather than judging only by the sticker price.

8. Texas A&M University

Texas A&M is one of the best D1 track schools for students who want strong facilities, a large athletics culture and balanced event groups.

The Aggies can suit sprinters, jumpers, relay athletes and students who want the atmosphere of a major US campus. It is also a practical option for students looking at Texas-based universities.

If Texas is your preferred location, compare Texas A&M with Texas, Houston, Baylor and Texas Tech before making your final list.

9. Auburn University

Auburn is a strong option for sprinters and hurdlers.

It competes in one of the toughest track and field environments in the country and has shown strong recent performance. For some athletes, Auburn may offer a better recruiting fit than a more crowded programme.

That is why rankings should guide you, not decide for you.

Sometimes the best track school is the one where the coach needs your exact event.

10. Stanford University

Stanford gives student-athletes one of the strongest academic-athletic combinations in the US.

It is a good fit for exceptional students, especially distance runners and athletes who want elite academics with serious sport. The support system and long-term academic value are strong.

The challenge is admission. Stanford is highly selective, so treat it as an ambitious target unless your academics and athletics are both excellent.

Students comparing elite US options can also review broader university choices for international applicants.

Five More Strong Track and Field Colleges to Consider

The top 10 list is useful, but it should not close your search. These five colleges strengthen the shortlist for students searching beyond “top 10 track and field colleges”.

University of Washington

Washington is a strong pick for distance and middle-distance runners. It also gives students a respected academic environment in Seattle.

Living costs can be high, so international students should calculate housing, food and insurance before committing.

University of Texas at Austin

Texas has facilities, history, academic strength and one of the biggest athletics brands in the country.

It suits students who want a large public university with strong sports culture and career opportunities. Texas is a serious option, but event fit still matters.

University of New Mexico

New Mexico is worth attention for distance and cross-country athletes.

It may not always appear high in general lists, but endurance athletes should not build their shortlist from sprint-heavy rankings.

Grand Valley State University

Grand Valley State is one of the best Division 2 track and field colleges for students who want strong competition and a realistic route to compete early.

For developing athletes, this can be a smarter pathway than sitting deep on a D1 roster.

West Texas A&M University

West Texas A&M is a strong Division II option, especially for women’s track and field.

It may also be more affordable than many private Division I universities. For international students, that can make the whole plan more realistic.

Many students search for “best track and field colleges D1” because Division I is the highest NCAA level.

Strong D1 options include:

Division I can be excellent, but it is not automatically the right route. If you receive little aid, rarely compete and struggle academically, a Division II or academically strong Division III option may serve you better.

Best Division 2 Track and Field Colleges

Division II is often underrated.

For many students, D2 offers strong competition, possible athletic aid and a more realistic route to compete early. This matters for international athletes who need both affordability and development time.

Good Division II options include:

  • Grand Valley State University
  • West Texas A&M University
  • Colorado School of Mines
  • Pittsburg State University
  • Adams State University
  • Minnesota State University
  • Angelo State University

Colorado School of Mines is especially interesting for students who want athletics alongside engineering, science or technical subjects. Students considering sport, health and performance-related degrees can also compare universities with sports medicine pathways.

A 400m hurdler should not copy a 5,000m runner’s list. A high jumper should not choose only from sprint rankings.

Think about it this way: college coaches recruit event gaps, not search keywords.

Track and Field Scholarships in USA

Track and field scholarships in USA are often partial.

That surprises many families.

A full ride can happen, but most athletes do not receive one automatically. Coaches divide scholarship money across a squad. One athlete may receive a large package. Another may receive a smaller percentage. Another may start as a walk-on and earn aid later.

Your scholarship chance depends on:

  • your event
  • your personal best
  • your academic profile
  • the team’s roster need
  • the coach’s budget
  • whether academic aid can combine with athletic aid

Under the current NCAA Division I model, roster and scholarship rules have changed for many programmes. According to the College Sports Commission roster limits, institutions subject to or opting into the House settlement have a roster limit of 45 athletes for both men’s and women’s outdoor track and field.

The short answer is simple: more flexibility does not mean every athlete gets a full scholarship.

Best Colleges for Track and Field Scholarships

The best colleges for track and field scholarships are not always the highest-ranked teams.

A top team may already have enough athletes in your event. A slightly less famous school may offer a better conversation because it needs your exact profile.

Strong scholarship conversations can happen at:

  • Arkansas
  • Florida
  • Georgia
  • LSU
  • Oregon
  • Tennessee
  • Texas A&M
  • Auburn
  • USC
  • Grand Valley State
  • West Texas A&M
  • Colorado School of Mines

For Bangladeshi students, it is useful to compare athletic aid with broader US scholarship planning, especially when tuition, housing and insurance all affect the final cost.

Add housing, meals, books, health insurance, flights and personal spending. For international students, health cover can be a real cost, so check what medical cover usually involves in the US before finalising your budget.

Use official university pages and the College Scorecard to compare cost, graduation rate and likely value.

How International Student-Athletes Can Apply

International student-athletes need to prepare earlier than domestic students.

The NCAA’s international eligibility steps ask international student-athletes to register with the Eligibility Center, understand academic and amateurism requirements, and submit the required documentation.

Follow this route:

  1. Prepare an athletics CV with your event, personal best, competition date, video and academic results.
  2. Shortlist colleges by event fit, not only ranking.
  3. Email coaches with a short, data-led message.
  4. Register with the NCAA Eligibility Center if you plan to compete in NCAA Division I or II.
  5. Prepare transcripts and certified translations if needed.

A useful coach email is clear, not dramatic.

Example:

My 400m personal best is 47.90, set on 12 May 2026. I graduate in 2027, have attached my academic record and included race video below.

That kind of message works because it gives the coach what they need fast.

Students who want help connecting admission documents, eligibility and coach communication can get support for international applications or talk through a shortlist through a free consultation.

D1 vs D2 vs D3: Which Division Is Best?

Division I is best for athletes who can compete at the highest college level and handle intense training, travel, roster competition and academic pressure.

Division II can be better for athletes who want strong competition, possible scholarships and a more realistic chance to compete early.

Division III does not offer athletic scholarships, but many D3 colleges are academically strong and may provide merit or need-based financial aid.

NAIA and junior college routes can also work for students who need development time, lower costs or a stepping-stone path.

Do not chase the highest division. Chase the right fit.

Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Track and Field College

Before applying, ask these questions:

Question

Why It Matters

Does the coach need my event?

Recruiting depends on roster gaps.

How many athletes are already in my event group?

Too much depth can reduce competition chances.

What is the total cost after aid?

Sticker price is not the real cost.

Can I study my chosen subject?

Athletics should not block your degree.

Will I compete as a first-year student?

Training without meets can slow development.

Is scholarship aid renewable?

Some awards change each year.

What support exists for international students?

If you are still comparing the US with other destinations, start from the wider study abroad pathway and then decide whether American college sport fits your academic and athletic goals.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best track and field colleges in the US?

The best track and field colleges in the US include Arkansas, Georgia, Oregon, Florida, LSU, Tennessee, USC, Texas A&M, Auburn, Stanford, Washington, Texas, New Mexico, Grand Valley State and West Texas A&M.

What are the top 10 track and field colleges in the US?

The top 10 track and field colleges in this guide are Arkansas, Georgia, Oregon, Florida, LSU, Tennessee, USC, Texas A&M, Auburn and Stanford.

What are the best D1 track and field colleges?

The best D1 track and field colleges include Arkansas, Georgia, Oregon, Florida, LSU, Tennessee, USC, Texas A&M, Auburn, Stanford, Washington and Texas.

What college has the best track team?

For current men’s outdoor performance, Arkansas is one of the strongest. For women’s outdoor performance, Georgia is one of the strongest. The best team for you still depends on your event, cost and scholarship fit.

What are the best track colleges for sprinters?

Florida, LSU, USC, Arkansas, Auburn and Texas A&M are strong options for sprinters and relay athletes.

Which colleges are best for distance runners?

Oregon, Stanford, Washington, New Mexico and BYU are strong choices for distance and cross-country athletes.

What are the best colleges for track and field scholarships?

There is no single best college for scholarships. Strong options include Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, LSU, Oregon, Tennessee, Texas A&M, Auburn, USC and selected Division II programmes. Your event and performance level matter most.

Can international students get track and field scholarships in USA?

Yes. International students can receive track and field scholarships in USA, but awards are competitive and often partial. Athletes need strong marks, academic records and early coach communication.

Can I get a full ride for track and field?

Yes, but full rides are rare. Coaches usually reserve major scholarship packages for athletes who can score at conference or national level.

Is Division II good for track and field?

Yes. Division II can be excellent for athletes who want strong competition, possible aid and more realistic competition chances.

When should I contact college coaches?

Final Advice

Start with the rankings. Then get specific.

The best track and field colleges in the US are not only the schools with trophies. They are the schools where your event, academics, budget and coach interest meet in one place.

A famous programme can impress you.

The right programme gives you a lane.
